text: Bitcoin is trading back above $81,000 today, and the story behind that number is really about the market shrugging off a rough patch rather than riding one clean trend. Two things hit crypto hard in the same week: the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in three years, lifting its target range to 3.75-4.00%, and the CLARITY Act's failure to clear a key Senate procedural vote, which dealt crypto's push for clear US regulation a real setback. That one-two punch briefly knocked Bitcoin below $76,000 and drove roughly $750 million out of spot Bitcoin ETFs over two days. But the selling didn't stick -- by Friday, ETF buyers came roaring back with the strongest single-day inflow in weeks, and Bitcoin snapped straight back above $81,000, a recovery that speaks to real underlying demand rather than just short-covering. Under the surface, the technical picture backs that up too: Bitcoin's 50-day average has crossed above its 200-day average for the first time since last November, a golden cross that traders read as a sign the longer-term trend is turning up. The next real test is the roughly $82,600 resistance level -- a clean break above that could open the door toward $98,000-$100,000, while a failure to clear it risks another round of the same choppy back-and-forth seen this week. None of this is a sure thing, but the pattern of bad news getting bought rather than sold is generally the more bullish tell right now.
